title: Albuterol Inhalation Solution, USP 0.083%: prescribing information
journal: US Food and Drug Administration, approved labelling; DailyMed structured product labelling version 20, published 30 April 2026, text dated February 2026
funder: Ritedose Pharmaceuticals, LLC markets the product and submits the labelling text; the US Food and Drug Administration approves it.
result: Indicated for relief of bronchospasm from 2 years of age; usual dose 2.5 mg three to four times daily by nebulisation. In asthmatic patients less than 20% of a nebulised or IPPB dose was absorbed, the remainder being recovered from the apparatus and expired air; after 3 mg nebulised, the maximum plasma level at 0.5 h was 2.1 ng/ml (range 1.4 to 3.2). In children, single doses of 3, 4 or 10 mg gave peak expiratory flow improvement comparable to 2 mg, but doses above 3 mg raised heart rate by more than 10%. Repeated dosing with 0.15 mg/kg in initially normokalaemic children aged 5 to 17 years was associated with an asymptomatic 20% to 25% fall in serum potassium. In clinical trials in 135 patients, drug-related effects were tremor 20%, dizziness 7%, nervousness 4%, headache 3%, nausea 4%, bronchospasm 8%, tachycardia 1% and hypertension 1%. Fatalities have been reported with excessive use of inhaled sympathomimetics and with home use of nebulisers. Postmarketing reports include urticaria, angioedema, oropharyngeal oedema, arrhythmias including atrial fibrillation, supraventricular tachycardia and extrasystoles, and metabolic acidosis. In isolated overdosage cases in children aged 2 to 12 years, heart rates above 200 beats/min were observed.
